body.statement: Using the rectangular hypergeometric stabilizer handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{unbal}}\), characterize the schedule-universal profile-equivalence classes and maximal common bijection group for complete randomization with \(n_1\neq n_0\), and determine the smallest uniform heterogeneous-unit separator bound as a function of \((n_1,n_0,K)\).
body.justification: Unequal allocation removes treatment complementation, so the first identity supporting balanced transposition disappears and a genuinely new frontier is required.
body.gap: \cite{ChungRomano2013} treats unequal proportions asymptotically and \cite{AronowChangLopatto2025} finds a computational balance split, but neither gives the exact fixed-schedule equivalence partition.
body.consumer: The answer would extend the software validation rule to trials whose realized or planned treatment count is not one half of the population.
